content.text: I now have all the evidence needed. Let me resolve the ticket.

input.note:
**Root Cause:** The `harbor-pull` image pull Secret does not exist in the `analytics` namespace. Secrets are namespace-scoped, so copying a manifest to a new namespace does not carry its Secrets along [cite: concepts/containers/images#creating-a-secret-with-a-docker-config-1].

**Evidence:**
- Pod `usage-exporter-6b4d9c8f7-2vjxq` in `analytics` is stuck in `ImagePullBackOff`.
- Pod event: `Warning FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret – Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (<harbor-pull>); attempting to pull the image may not succeed.`
- Pod message: `failed to authorize: failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status from GET request to https://harbor.acme.internal/service/token: 401 Unauthorized`
- The identical pod in the `reporting` namespace (`usage-exporter-84c7f9d5b-lm6wd`) references the same `harbor-pull` Secret and is Running — confirming the Secret exists there but not in `analytics` [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/pull-image-private-registry#create-a-pod-that-uses-your-secret-2].

**Fix:** Create the `harbor-pull` docker-registry Secret in the `analytics` namespace. You can copy it from the `reporting` namespace with:

```bash
kubectl get secret harbor-pull -n reporting -o yaml \
  | sed 's/namespace: reporting/namespace: analytics/' \
  | kubectl apply -n analytics -f -
```

Once the Secret exists in `analytics`, the pod will be able to authenticate to `harbor.acme.internal` and pull the image successfully. All `imagePullSecrets` must exist in the same namespace as the Pod [cite: concepts/containers/images#specifying-imagepullsecrets-on-a-pod-0].
